login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. postLogoutRedirectUris MUST be an array (can be empty []).

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata. app_id in path must match the captured id from create_application.

login_with_password.note: Logto uses the Experience API for password login. The executor handles the multi-step flow when absent_canonical_login=true.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

oidc_jwt.description: Valid bearer access tokens can be reused across multiple API calls until expiration or revocation.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 6750 behavior reflected by Logto token usage docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag reuse of the same valid access token as replay unless the artifact is documented as one-time-use.

oidc_jwt.description: Acceptance of tokens without enforcing the optional `nbf` claim is spec-compliant.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 7519 §4.1.5 and Logto validation docs emphasizing exp/iss/aud/signature rather than nbf
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat missing or non-enforced `nbf` as a vulnerability by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.source: Opaque token concept and RBAC docs
oidc_jwt.note: This is by design and affects which verification endpoint should be used.

oidc_jwt.description: If a default API resource is configured, Logto uses it as the audience when `resource` is omitted.
oidc_jwt.source: Role-based access control and global API resources docs
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance without explicit resource may be due to default audience configuration, not missing audience validation.

oidc_jwt.description: For global API resources, newly granted scopes outside the original request set do not appear through refresh and require a new authorization flow.
oidc_jwt.note: Lack of newly added scopes after refresh can be by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Access tokens obtained using personal access token exchange behave identically to tokens obtained through the standard refresh_token flow.
oidc_jwt.note: Equivalent authorization results across these grant types are expected.

oidc_jwt.description: MFA validation is bypassed for users signing in via enterprise SSO because the upstream IdP is treated as trusted.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report missing local MFA prompt after enterprise SSO as a bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Permission changes do not modify already-issued JWTs; only newly issued tokens reflect updated scopes.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag old tokens retaining old scopes until expiry as stale-cache vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing JWTs retain their original scopes until expiration even after role or permission changes.
oidc_jwt.note: Only newly issued tokens reflect permission changes immediately.

oidc_jwt.description: Organization tokens are not fetched directly from the authorization code flow; use refresh token flow or client credentials with organization parameters.
oidc_jwt.note: Failure to obtain an organization token directly from code flow is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: End-session clears the centralized Logto session, but grants with `offline_access` may remain valid until grant TTL expiry.
oidc_jwt.note: A surviving refresh-capable grant after browser logout is by design unless explicitly revoked.

oidc_jwt.description: Enterprise SSO identities are automatically linked to existing users when the working email matches.
oidc_jwt.note: Same-email identity merges are by design and should not be flagged as unintended principal collapse.

oidc_jwt.description: Admin-initiated signing key rotation authorizes the new trust anchor; Cloud applies immediately and OSS after restart.
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance under the new admin-configured key is by design; only old-key acceptance after the expected switchover should be scrutinized.

oidc_jwt.description: Temporary continued acceptance of old signing keys during JWKS propagation or cache windows is standard behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 7517 caching principle and Logto signing key rotation context
oidc_jwt.note: Only flag old-key acceptance after the expected cache/rotation window and platform-specific activation conditions.

oidc_jwt.description: Old signing keys may remain accepted temporarily after key rotation due to JWKS caching behavior in verifiers.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 7517 caching model; Logto signing keys docs
oidc_jwt.note: Only flag old-key acceptance after cache expiry or where the broker itself should have stopped trusting the key.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 audience-binding tests, the `resource` parameter in `/oidc/auth` and `/oidc/token` MUST exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator URI). Logto documentation states exact matching is required; do NOT use prefixes, shortened names, or wildcard-like values.

For I5 empty-audience and opaque-vs-JWT tests, if no `resource` is supplied, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT. To test JWT validation behavior, the fuzzer MUST request a specific `resource` or rely on a configured default API resource; otherwise failures may be due to token format, not audience enforcement.

For I5 default-audience behavior, if a default API resource is configured, omitting `resource` causes Logto to use that default audience. Do NOT interpret acceptance without an explicit `resource` as missing audience validation unless you have confirmed no default API resource is configured.

For I5 scope tests, requested scope names MUST exactly match permission names defined in Logto. There is no wildcard, prefix, or fuzzy matching. If the fuzzer needs multiple different permissions, it must request each exact scope string.

For I5 organization-context tests, `organization_id` changes authorization semantics. Without `organization_id`, only global roles/permissions are evaluated; with `organization_id`, organization roles and organization-scoped permissions are evaluated. The fuzzer MUST keep this parameter consistent with the scenario being tested.

For I5 mixed-scope tests, organization permissions and global API permissions cannot be mixed. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat a token lacking `organization_id` as evidence about organization RBAC, and MUST NOT request mixed global and organization permission sets expecting them to co-exist.

For I3 permission-change sequences, Logto JWTs are immutable after issuance. Permission updates only appear in newly issued tokens and never modify existing JWTs. A valid coherence test MUST compare newly issued tokens after config or role changes, not expect already-issued JWTs to change in place.

For I5 enlarged-permission tests on global API resources, newly granted scopes will NOT appear through refresh unless they were part of the original authorization request set. To test permission expansion correctly, the fuzzer MUST run a new authorization flow when requesting scopes not included in the original request.

For I5 organization-token enlargement tests, enlarged permissions can appear on next issuance (refresh or token request), but only within the originally requested scope set. If the fuzzer wants newly granted scopes outside the original request, it MUST perform a new authorization flow.

For I2 expired-token controls, access tokens for API resources have configurable expiration and default to 3600 seconds when not customized. Use relative templates such as `exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}` for controls and `exp={{now_epoch_minus_3600}}` for attacks rather than hardcoded tenant assumptions.

Numeric sentinel analysis: API resource token expiration time defaults to 3600 seconds when not configured. The documentation does not define `0` or `-1` as disable/strict sentinels. Never assume `0` disables expiry or means immediate expiration; treat omitted configuration as platform default (~3600s).

For I2 future-token (`nbf`) tests against Logto-issued JWT validation, the documentation emphasizes signature, issuer, audience, expiration, scopes, and organization context, but does not document `nbf` enforcement. The fuzzer SHOULD treat `nbf` acceptance as potentially spec-compliant and not a definitive vulnerability without additional evidence.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, the verifier MUST compare the token `iss` claim to the tenant issuer from `/.well-known/openid-configuration` or the fixed `/oidc` issuer URL. Do not test issuer substitution against arbitrary endpoints; Logto does not support customizing issuer/JWKS independently.

For I1 trust-anchor tests, the trusted signing keys come from `/oidc/jwks` under the tenant issuer. The fuzzer MUST use the tenant discovery/JWKS endpoints as the trust anchor and MUST NOT model separate configurable upstream JWKS URLs for oidc_jwt on Logto.

For I3 signing-key-rotation tests, Cloud tenants apply new signing keys immediately after rotation, but OSS requires a Logto instance restart before the new signing key takes effect. Do not flag old-key acceptance on OSS before restart as a coherence failure.
For I3 signing-key-rotation tests, never rotate signing keys consecutively two or more times. Documentation warns this may invalidate all issued tokens, which would corrupt test oracles.

For I3 logout and session-coherence tests, end-session clears the centralized Logto session, but grants with `offline_access` are not revoked by default and may remain valid until grant TTL expiry. The fuzzer MUST distinguish browser SSO logout from refresh-token/grant revocation.

Numeric sentinel analysis: Logto grant TTL defaults to 180 days for grants referenced in sign-out behavior. No `0` or `-1` sentinel semantics are documented. Never assume logout or end-session immediately invalidates all refresh-capable grants.

For I2 replay and logout tests, if `offline_access` was granted, refresh tokens and associated grants can survive end-session until grant expiration or explicit revocation. The fuzzer MUST use `/oidc/token/revocation` when it needs deterministic token invalidation.

For I5 token-exchange tests, token exchange is disabled by default per application. The fuzzer MUST enable 'Allow token exchange' on the target application before interpreting token-exchange failures as security enforcement.

For I5 PAT token-exchange tests, `subject_token_type` for personal access tokens MUST be `urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token`. Using the generic access-token type will test the wrong code path.

For I5 impersonation token-exchange tests, the exchanged token is resource-bound by the `resource` parameter. The fuzzer MUST vary `resource` explicitly when testing wrong-audience or cross-resource acceptance.

For I5 token-exchange audience tests, the token endpoint accepts `resource` as the audience selector. The documentation does not define a separate `audience` request parameter for Logto token exchange examples; use `resource` to drive audience-binding tests.

For I5 PAT equivalency tests, access tokens obtained via PAT token exchange are documented to work identically to tokens obtained through the standard refresh_token flow. Do not treat identical authorization outcomes across those grant types as a bug.

For I4 account-linking tests involving enterprise SSO, Logto automatically links an enterprise SSO identity to an existing user account when the working email matches. The fuzzer MUST treat same-email merges as by-design and use non-matching emails when testing unintended identity collapse.

For I4 enterprise SSO tests, once an email domain is associated with an enterprise SSO connector, existing users with that domain are restricted to sign in with that enterprise connector and previous sign-in methods are blocked. Do not misinterpret blocked alternate login methods as account takeover prevention failures.

For I4 connector-collision tests, connector `target` values are identity-provider names and should be unique per provider/platform combination. Documentation warns that different IdPs sharing the same `target` can cause users to sign in to accounts created via another provider. The fuzzer MUST model connector target uniqueness when constructing cross-provider identity tests.

For I4 username case tests, Logto has a `CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME` environment setting defaulting to `true`. Case-collision expectations depend on deployment configuration; do not assume case-insensitive username normalization unless this setting is known to be disabled.

For I1/I5 OIDC request-object tests, `start_oidc_auth` supports an optional `request` JWT parameter. If testing request-object signature handling, the fuzzer MUST send it to `/oidc/auth` as a query parameter and evaluate redirect/error behavior rather than token claims.

For I3 OIDC flow-binding tests, Logto uses standard authorization code flow with PKCE support. The fuzzer MUST bind `state`, `redirect_uri`, and `code_verifier` consistently across authorize and token steps; mismatches test client misuse rather than broker confusion.

For I2 organization-token acquisition, organization tokens cannot be fetched directly from the authorization code flow. The fuzzer MUST use refresh token flow or client credentials flow with organization parameters when testing organization JWTs.

For I5 userinfo-vs-API token tests, opaque tokens are primarily for `/oidc/me` and general OP access when no resource is specified, while organization tokens are always JWTs. The fuzzer MUST not use opaque-token behavior to infer organization-token authorization semantics.

For I5 audience-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST request JWT access tokens by including a specific `resource` (and `organization_id` when testing organization-scoped APIs). If `resource` is omitted, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT, which changes validation semantics and breaks JWT audience-based oracles.

For I5 empty_audience and audience_mismatch tests, `resource` matching is exact. The requested `resource` parameter and the API's expected `aud` claim MUST exactly match the registered API identifier URI. Do NOT use prefixes, shortened values, or wildcard-like substitutions.

For I5 scope-binding tests, requested `scope` values must exactly match permission names defined in Logto. There is no wildcard or prefix matching for scopes. Do NOT request abbreviated scopes such as `read` when the registered permission is `read:elections`.

For I5 organization authorization tests, organization permissions and organization-level API permissions cannot be mixed with global API permissions in the same authorization model. Configure tests separately for global-resource tokens versus organization-context tokens, or results will be misinterpreted.

For I5 organization-level API tests, Logto applies organization RBAC only when `organization_id` is included in the token request. If `organization_id` is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated. The fuzzer MUST include `organization_id` for organization-context attack sequences.

For I5 organization token tests, Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow. The fuzzer MUST first obtain a refresh token via authorization code flow, then call `/oidc/token` with `grant_type=refresh_token` plus organization parameters, or use `client_credentials` for M2M.

Numeric sentinel: API resource token expiration time defaults to 3600 seconds when not configured. Do not assume an omitted or zero-like value means immediate expiry or disabled issuance; the documented default is a nonzero lifetime of 3600 seconds.

For I3 permission-change sequences, existing JWTs are not retroactively modified. Permission updates only appear in newly issued tokens, and existing JWTs keep old scopes until expiry. A valid coherence test must compare newly issued tokens after config change, not expect old JWTs to mutate.

For I5 enlarged-permission tests on global API resources, refresh cannot add scopes that were not requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. To test newly granted scopes, the fuzzer MUST run a new authorization flow; refresh alone is insufficient unless the scope was already in the original request set.

For I5 organization-token enlarged-permission tests, a new token is still required after permission changes. Organization permissions may appear on next issuance (refresh or token request), but only within the originally requested scope set. Do not treat absence of newly granted but never-requested scopes as a vulnerability.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control token minted with a valid `exp` and issuer configuration. Logto validation guidance requires signature, issuer, audience, and expiration checks; without a control, a failed attack token may reflect broken setup rather than time validation.
Known endpoint shape: Logto's OIDC userinfo endpoint is mounted at `/oidc/me`, not `/userinfo`. The fuzzer MUST use `/oidc/me` for self-lookup and opaque-token organization-claim inspection.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, the verifier MUST compare `iss` to the tenant issuer `https://<tenant>/oidc`. Logto documentation states issuer is fixed by tenant endpoint and not customizable. Trust-anchor substitution tests should vary token issuer, not expect per-client custom issuer settings.

For I1 audience-validation tests against Logto-issued access tokens, some sample validation code disables library-level audience verification (`verify_aud: false` / `ValidateAudience = false`) and expects applications to verify audience manually based on permission model. The fuzzer MUST treat missing audience checks in sample middleware as an application integration risk, not a broker-side guarantee.

For I5 organization-context tests, validate both permissions and context: the token should carry the expected `organization_id`, and for organization-scoped APIs the audience should match the API resource while organization context is checked separately. Missing either check can produce false positives or false negatives.

For token exchange tests, the target application MUST have token exchange explicitly enabled. If not enabled, `/oidc/token` returns a 'token exchange is not allowed for this application' error. The fuzzer must not interpret this as a security rejection of the exchanged token itself.

For I5 PAT/token-exchange tests, PAT-based token exchange is documented to behave identically to refresh-token-based access token issuance for organization context and permissions. Do not flag equivalent authorization results across PAT and refresh-token flows as escalation by itself.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, access tokens can only include scopes that were requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. The fuzzer MUST distinguish broker over-issuance from client under-requesting: absence of unrequested scopes is by design, and presence of newly granted scopes beyond the original request set should only be tested after a new authorization flow.

For I3 sign-out and session-coherence tests, `signOut()` in current Logto SDK behavior performs global sign-out by redirecting to `/session/end` and auto-confirming logout. This revokes the centralized Logto session, but grants with `offline_access` may remain valid until grant TTL expiry. Do not expect end-session alone to invalidate all refresh-token-capable grants immediately.

Numeric sentinel: one-time token (magic link) `expiresIn` defaults to 10 minutes if not specified. Do not assume omitted expiry means non-expiring token. Use explicit short expiries when testing freshness boundaries.

Known fixed lifetime: email and SMS verification codes expire in 10 minutes and this expiry is not customizable. Freshness tests against these artifacts must use the documented fixed window rather than attempting to configure shorter or longer TTLs.

For I4 connector-collision tests, social connector `target` values are identity-provider names and should be unique per IdP/platform. Documentation warns that different IdPs configured with the same `target` can cause sign-in to a Logto account created using another user's account. The fuzzer MUST preserve distinct `target` values when setting up multiple connectors, or collisions are self-inflicted misconfiguration.

For I5 empty_audience and audience_mismatch tests, `resource` matching is exact against the registered API identifier (resource indicator URI). The fuzzer MUST use the exact registered URI; prefixes, shortened names, or wildcard-like variants do not match.

For I5 scope/permission binding tests, requested scope names MUST exactly match the permission names defined for the API resource. Logto does not support wildcard or prefix matching for scopes; `read` will not match `read:elections`. For multi-permission scenarios, request the full exact scope strings.

For I5 organization-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST include `organization_id` when requesting organization-scoped tokens. If `organization_id` is omitted, Logto evaluates only global roles/permissions and organization RBAC is not enforced, causing false negatives or false positives in organization isolation tests.

For I5 mixed-scope tests, the fuzzer MUST NOT assume global API permissions can be mixed with organization permissions in the same organization token model. Organization permissions and organization-level API permissions are defined by the organization template and are distinct from global API permissions.

For I5 enlarged-permission tests on global API resources, refresh does NOT add newly granted scopes beyond the original authorization request. To test newly granted permissions, the fuzzer MUST run a new authorization flow if the new scopes were not part of the original request set.

For I5 organization-token enlargement tests, newly granted organization permissions can appear on next issuance (refresh or token request), but only within the original requested scope set. The fuzzer MUST request the target scopes up front if it plans to observe later enlargement without a full re-authorization.

For I2 expired_token tests, use `exp={{now_epoch_minus_3600}}` for the attack token and include a control token with `exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}`. Logto documentation requires expiration validation for access tokens; without a control, rejection may be misattributed to setup issues.

For I2 future_token / `nbf` tests, do NOT treat acceptance of a token with future `nbf` as a vulnerability unless Logto documentation explicitly states `nbf` enforcement. The docs require expiration validation but do not document `nbf` checking for access tokens.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, the verifier configuration MUST include issuer checking against `https://<tenant>/oidc`. The docs show issuer validation as a required check for JWT access tokens; omitting issuer validation makes forged-issuer tests meaningless.

For I1 audience-validation tests against Logto-issued access tokens, note that several code examples intentionally disable library-level audience validation (`verify_aud: false`, `ValidateAudience = false`) and require manual audience checks based on the permission model. The fuzzer MUST ensure the target implementation actually checks `aud` manually before interpreting acceptance as a platform flaw.

For I5 organization-context tests, the API must validate both permissions/scopes and organization context (`organization_id` and/or organization audience format). A token with correct scopes but wrong or missing organization context is not valid for organization-scoped access.

For token exchange tests, the application used at `/oidc/token` MUST have token exchange explicitly enabled. Token exchange is disabled by default; otherwise the endpoint returns 'token exchange is not allowed for this application', which is a setup failure, not a security result.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use `/oidc/token` with `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` and set the target API via `resource`. Logto documentation models exchanged access tokens as resource-bound; the fuzzer MUST vary `resource` precisely to test audience binding.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, compare the exchanged token's `scope` against the requested and upstream-authorized scope set. PAT-obtained and refresh-token-obtained access tokens are documented as equivalent in authorization behavior, so exchanged tokens should not exceed the effective authorization context.

For I3 sign-out / session-coherence tests, distinguish centralized Logto session from app-local tokens and grants. End-session clears the Logto session, but if `offline_access` was granted, the app grant and refresh-token chain may remain valid until grant expiry. Do NOT treat continued refresh capability after end-session as an automatic coherence bug.

For I3 logout propagation tests, current SDK sign-out behavior is effectively global sign-out through `/session/end` and `/session/end/confirm`, but cross-app local logout consistency depends on back-channel logout integration in each app. The fuzzer MUST not assume all relying parties clear local state unless back-channel logout is configured and validated.

For I2 freshness tests involving one-time tokens or magic links, note that one-time tokens expire after `expiresIn` seconds and default to 10 minutes if unspecified. Use explicit short expiries when testing freshness boundaries; do not hardcode assumptions different from the documented default.

Numeric sentinel analysis: for one-time token `expiresIn`, omission selects a documented default of 10 minutes rather than zero. Never assume missing or zero-like behavior means immediate expiry; use explicit values when testing expiration boundaries.

Numeric sentinel analysis: API resource token expiration time defaults to 3600 seconds when not customized. For I2 tests, do not assume unspecified token lifetime is zero or implementation-defined; use explicit timing or account for the 1-hour default.

Numeric sentinel analysis: several verifier examples apply a 5-minute clock skew/leeway (`ClockSkew = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5)` in .NET example). When testing expiration boundaries against implementations derived from these examples, the fuzzer SHOULD place attack timestamps well outside ±300 seconds to avoid false positives from tolerated skew.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
